L0: # Prebid Sales Agent
L1: 
L2: An open-source implementation of the [Ad Context Protocol (AdCP)](https://adcontextprotocol.org)
L3: sales-agent role, maintained under Prebid.org. It lets AI agents discover and buy advertising
L4: inventory through standardized MCP and A2A interfaces.
L5: > **Status: alpha.** A pre-1.0 implementation of a pre-release protocol
L6: > (AdCP 3.1.1), under active development. APIs still change between
L7: > releases — `v2.0.0` introduced breaking changes — so pin a version and expect
L8: > to adapt on upgrade. It is one of several AdCP sales-agent implementations,
L9: > not a sole or canonical reference. The codebase is substantial and functional
L10: > (Google Ad Manager integration, multi-tenant isolation, 16 AdCP tools,
L11: > extensive tests), but treat it as alpha and validate before relying on it.
L12: ## What is this?
L13: 
L14: The Prebid Sales Agent is a server that:
L15: - **Exposes advertising inventory** to AI agents via MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent-to-Agent)
L16: - **Integrates with ad servers** like Google Ad Manager
L17: - **Provides an admin interface** for managing inventory and campaigns
L18: - **Handles the full campaign lifecycle** from discovery to reporting
L19: ## AdCP Compatibility
L20: 
L21: This implementation targets **AdCP spec version 3.1.1** via the `adcp==6.6.0`
L22: Python SDK. The protocol is pre-1.0 — request/response shapes still move between
L23: spec releases, and SDK bumps can change them. See
L24: [docs/adcp-spec-version.md](docs/adcp-spec-version.md) for the SDK-to-spec mapping
L25: and bump procedure. The pin is enforced by a CI guard
L26: (`tests/unit/test_adcp_spec_version.py`), which fails on drift.
L27: ## Choose Your Path
L28: 
L29: | I want to... | Start here |
L30: |--------------|------------|
L31: | **Deploy my own sales agent** (publisher) | [Quickstart Guide](docs/quickstart.md) |
L32: | **Evaluate or develop locally** | [Quick Start](#quick-start-evaluation) below |
L33: | **Run a multi-tenant platform** | [Deployment Guide](docs/deployment/multi-tenant.md) |
L34: 
L35: ---
L36: ## Quick Start (Evaluation)
L37: 
L38: Try the sales agent locally:
L39: 
L40: ```bash
L41: # Clone and start
L42: git clone https://github.com/prebid/salesagent.git
L43: cd salesagent
L44: docker compose up -d
L45: # Test the MCP interface
L46: uvx adcp http://localhost:8000/mcp/ --auth test-token list_tools
L47: uvx adcp http://localhost:8000/mcp/ --auth test-token get_products '{"brief":"video"}'
L48: ```
L49: 
L50: Access services at http://localhost:8000:
L51: - **Admin UI:** `/admin` or just click "Log in to Dashboard" (test credentials: `test123`)
L52: - **MCP Server:** `/mcp/`
L53: - **A2A Server:** `/a2a`
L54: 
L55: For production deployment, see the [Quickstart Guide](docs/quickstart.md).
L56: 
L57: ---
L58: ## Publisher Deployment
L59: 
L60: Publishers deploy their own sales agent. Choose based on your needs:
L61: | Platform | Time | Difficulty | Guide |
L62: |----------|------|------------|-------|
L63: | **Docker** (local/on-prem) | 2 min | Easy | [quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md) |
L64: | **Fly.io** (cloud) | 10-15 min | Medium | [fly.md](docs/deployment/walkthroughs/fly.md) |
L65: | **Google Cloud Run** | 15-20 min | Medium | [gcp.md](docs/deployment/walkthroughs/gcp.md) |
L66: | **AWS** (ECS Fargate, RDS) | 30 min | Medium | [aws.md](docs/deployment/aws.md) |
L67: | **Single VM** (Docker Compose + Caddy) | 30-45 min | Medium | [vm.md](docs/deployment/vm.md) |
L68: **Docker is the fastest** - it bundles PostgreSQL and just works. Cloud platforms require separate database setup.
L69: 
L70: The app itself is platform-agnostic — beyond the walkthroughs above you can host it anywhere:
L71: - Docker (recommended) — any Docker-compatible platform
L72: - Kubernetes — full k8s manifests supported
L73: - Cloud providers — AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean
L74: - Platform services — Fly.io, Heroku, Railway, Render
L75: 
L76: See `docs/deployment/` for platform-specific guides.
L77: Because this is alpha software tracking a beta protocol, pin the version you deploy
L78: and re-test after every upgrade — minor releases can carry breaking changes.
L79: ### After Deployment
L80: 
L81: Configure via the Admin UI:
L82: 1. Configure your ad server (Settings → Adapters)
L83: 2. Set up products that match your GAM line items
L84: 3. Add advertisers who will use the MCP API
L85: 4. Set your custom domain (Settings → General)
L86: 
L87: ---
L88: ## Development Setup
L89: 
L90: ```bash
L91: git clone https://github.com/prebid/salesagent.git
L92: cd salesagent
L93: make setup    # One command: installs deps, starts Docker, verifies health
L94: ```
L95: 
L96: See the [Getting Started guide](docs/development/GETTING_STARTED.md) for prerequisites, manual setup steps, testing workflows, and common operations.
L97: 
L98: ---
L99: ## Google Ad Manager Setup
L100: 
L101: For GAM integration, choose your authentication method:
L102: 
L103: **Service Account (Recommended for Production):**
L104: - No OAuth credentials needed
L105: - Configure service account JSON in Admin UI
L106: - See [GAM Adapter Guide](docs/adapters/gam/README.md) for setup
L107: **OAuth (Development/Testing):**
L108: 1. Create OAuth credentials at [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)
L109: 2. Add to .env:
L110:    ```bash
L111:    GAM_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
L112:    GAM_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
L113:    ```
L114: 3. Configure in Admin UI: Settings → Adapters → Google Ad Manager
L115: 
L116: ---
L117: ## Using with Claude Desktop
L118: 
L119: Add to your Claude config (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`):
L120: 
L121: ```json
L122: {
L123:   "mcpServers": {
L124:     "adcp": {
L125:       "command": "uvx",
L126:       "args": ["mcp-remote", "http://localhost:8000/mcp/", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"]
L127:     }
L128:   }
L129: }
L130: ```
L131: 
L132: Your token is shown once, when the advertiser is created in Admin UI → Advertisers; rotate it there if it is lost.
L133: 
L134: ---
L135: ## Troubleshooting
L136: 
L137: **Container won't start?**
L138: ```bash
L139: docker compose logs adcp-server | head -50
L140: ```
L141: 
L142: **GAM OAuth error?**
L143: - Verify `GAM_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `GAM_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env`
L144: - Restart: `docker compose restart`
L145: 
L146: **More help:** [Troubleshooting Guide](docs/development/troubleshooting.md)
L147: 
L148: ## Documentation
L149: ### Deployment Guides
L150: - **[Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md)** - Docker deployment (2 min)
L151: - **[Fly.io](docs/deployment/walkthroughs/fly.md)** - Cloud deployment (10-15 min)
L152: - **[Google Cloud Run](docs/deployment/walkthroughs/gcp.md)** - GCP deployment (15-20 min)
L153: - **[AWS](docs/deployment/aws.md)** - ECS Fargate, RDS and ALB with Terraform (30 min)
L154: - **[Single VM](docs/deployment/vm.md)** - Docker Compose and Caddy on one Linux VM, multi-tenant
L155: - **[Single-Tenant](docs/deployment/single-tenant.md)** - Single publisher deployment
L156: - **[Multi-Tenant](docs/deployment/multi-tenant.md)** - Platform deployment
L157: ### Reference
L158: - **[Development Guide](docs/development/README.md)** - Local development and contributing
L159: - **[Architecture](docs/development/architecture.md)** - System design and database schema
L160: - **[Troubleshooting Guide](docs/development/troubleshooting.md)** - Monitoring and debugging
L161: ## AdCP Tools
L162: 
L163: The MCP server exposes 16 AdCP tools (registered in
L164: [`src/core/main.py`](src/core/main.py)). The server also exposes AdCP operations over A2A as JSON-RPC skills; the exact set differs slightly from the MCP tool list.

L0: # Agentic Mobile
L1: 
L2: An open standard for AI agents to orchestrate mobile in-app advertising workflows.
L3: 
L4: [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
L5: [![Spec Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/spec-v1.0.0--draft-orange.svg)](docs/specification.md)
L6: ## Overview
L7: 
L8: Agentic Mobile enables AI agents to discover, configure, and optimize mobile advertising supply and demand. Built for the agentic era, it provides standardized interfaces for programmatic communication between intelligent agents and mobile advertising platforms.
L9: **Multi-Protocol Support:**
L10: - **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) - Direct AI assistant integration via stdio or HTTP
L11: - **A2A** (Agent2Agent Protocol) - Agent-to-agent workflows with task management
L12: - **REST API** - Traditional integrations (planned)
L13: ### Why Agentic Mobile?
L14: 
L15: Mobile in-app advertising has unique requirements:
L16: 
L17: - **SDK-based environments** with initialization and configuration needs
L18: - **Real-time auction dynamics** with sub-200ms latency requirements
L19: - **Platform-specific privacy** (ATT, Privacy Sandbox, SKAdNetwork)
L20: - **Complex mediation** across multiple ad networks
L21: - **Gradual rollouts** tied to app release cycles
L22: 
L23: Agentic Mobile addresses these with a protocol designed specifically for mobile.
L24: ## Protocol Structure
L25: ```
L26: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
L27: │                       Agentic Mobile v1                            │
L28: ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
L29: │                                                              │
L30: │  ACCESS METHODS                                              │
L31: │  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐             │
L32: │  │    MCP     │  │    A2A     │  │    REST    │             │
L33: │  │  (stdio)   │  │   (HTTP)   │  │  (planned) │             │
L34: │  └────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────┘             │
L35: │                                                              │
L36: │  SUPPLY SIDE (v1)                                            │
L37: │  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐             │
L38: │  │ Inventory  │  │  Pricing   │  │ Reporting  │             │
L39: │  │            │  │            │  │            │             │
L40: │  │ • Apps     │  │ • Rules    │  │ • Summary  │             │
L41: │  │ • Places   │  │ • Deals    │  │ • Breakdown│             │
L42: │  │ • Networks │  │ • Tests    │  │            │             │
L43: │  │ • Config   │  │ • Lists    │  │            │             │
L44: │  └────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────┘             │
L45: │                                                              │
L46: │  DEMAND SIDE (v2 - Planned)                                  │
L47: │  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐                             │
L48: │  │  Campaigns │  │  Creative  │                             │
L49: │  └────────────┘  └────────────┘                             │
L50: │                                                              │
L51: └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
L52: ```
L53: ## Supply Side Protocols (v1)
L54: ### Inventory Protocol
L55: 
L56: Manage mobile apps, ad placements, network configurations, and SDK settings.
L57: | Task | Description |
L58: |------|-------------|
L59: | `inventory/list_apps` | List apps with filtering |
L60: | `inventory/get_app` | Get app details |
L61: | `inventory/create_app` | Create new app |
L62: | `inventory/update_app` | Update app configuration |
L63: | `inventory/list_placements` | List ad placements |
L64: | `inventory/create_placement` | Create new placement |
L65: | `inventory/update_placement` | Update placement configuration |
L66: | `inventory/get_sdk_config` | Get SDK initialization config |
L67: ### Pricing Protocol
L68: 
L69: Configure pricing rules, private deals, block lists, and run A/B experiments.
L70: | Task | Description |
L71: |------|-------------|
L72: | `pricing/list_rules` | List pricing rules |
L73: | `pricing/create_rule` | Create pricing rule |
L74: | `pricing/update_rule` | Update pricing rule |
